what: Marsh is the world's largest insurance broker. It arranges insurance and reinsurance for companies, advises on risk, and through Mercer advises on pensions and benefits. It does not take insurance risk itself.
customers: Large and mid-sized companies, public bodies and insurers needing reinsurance.
money: insurance broking and reinsurance broking through Guy Carpenter
pension and benefits advice through Mercer, and management consulting
moat: Client relationships that renew every year, data on pricing across the market, and scale that smaller brokers cannot match in complex risks.
risks: Commission income falls when insurance prices soften after a hard market
Acquisitions have added debt of about $21 billion
Consulting demand weakens in a downturn
Regulators periodically examine broker commission arrangements
opportunities: Revenue is largely recurring because policies renew annually
Growth in cyber, climate and political risk creates demand for advice
It takes no underwriting risk, so earnings are far steadier than an insurer's
watch: Underlying revenue growth, which strips out acquisitions and currency.
